input.direction: Copy-only pass for a meeting-notes tool: plain, mechanism-led sentences carrying the premium register through precision rather than adjectives, since no customers/metrics/integrations exist to prove a bigger claim.

hierarchy: Promise: a recorded meeting becomes a usable Markdown record
Mechanism: upload triggers transcription (German or English) then Markdown export with action items
Empty state: no recordings yet, upload prompts the same mechanism

claims.text: Transcribes an uploaded recording in German or English
Exports a Markdown file with action items
Customers, metrics, funding, certifications, integrations, launch date
claims.evidence: None exist; excluded from copy rather than invented

localization: All shipped strings are English; German is a transcription output language, not a localized UI, so locale-de was not loaded.
No idiom, wordplay, or color-only meaning used, so no transcreation risk to flag.

lines: Turn a recorded meeting into a Markdown file with action items.
Upload the recording. Get a transcript in German or English, plus a Markdown file with the action items pulled out.
Upload a recording in German or English and get a transcript alongside a Markdown export listing every action item, ready to drop into your notes tool.
No recordings yet. Upload one to get a transcript and a Markdown export with action items.
slopChecks: Mode: rewrite (drafted directly against the ledger, not audited after the fact).
Tier 1: zero hits — no negative parallelism, no colon reveal, no rhetorical question, no fake-profound kicker, no vague attribution.
Tier 2: zero hits — 'innovative' and 'premium' (the founder's brief words) were not used; no delve/leverage/seamless/robust/unlock-family vocabulary anywhere in the five lines.
Tier 3 em dash: 0 per ~70 words (budget ≤1 per 300).
Tier 3 evaluative adjectives: 0 per line (budget ≤1 per headline/blurb sentence) — lines carry the claim on nouns/verbs (transcript, Markdown, action items, upload).

Specificity floor: every line names the mechanism (upload → transcript → Markdown export) and a named object (Markdown file, action items); headline swap test passes as a deliberate category claim since transcription + Markdown export is the entire verified feature set, not a placeholder for something bigger.
Empty state follows content-design microcopy: names condition (no recordings yet) and next step (upload one), no apology theatre.
Linter not run — no lint-copy.mjs invocation available in this text-only exchange; findings above are manual per the Tier-1/2/3 catalogue.

responsive.wide: Hero headline and subhead stack left-aligned above the fold with the primary CTA directly beneath; feature blurb sits in a single adjacent block, not a card grid of one.
responsive.portrait: Same vertical order full-width; subhead line-wraps at the natural clause break after 'the recording.' rather than mid-phrase.
responsive.narrow: Headline, subhead, CTA, feature blurb, then empty state remain in strict single-column source order with no truncation of the Markdown/action-items mechanism.
recomposition: CTA stays adjacent to the subhead at every width so the promised action is never separated from the promise.
Feature blurb never collapses into a card row; it stays prose to avoid implying a multi-feature set that doesn't exist.
Empty state copy is unabridged at narrow width since it is the only content shown pre-upload.
responsive.sourceOrder: headline → subhead → primary CTA → feature blurb → empty state, unchanged across breakpoints

contrastStates: Hero headline/subhead text meets body/heading contrast against its background in both light and dark modes.
Primary CTA label text meets contrast in default, hover, focus, and disabled states.
Empty-state copy meets contrast at the reduced visual weight typically given to placeholder/empty content.
inputParity: Primary CTA is reachable and activatable by keyboard with a visible focus state, matching pointer behavior.
Empty-state upload prompt exposes the same action to keyboard and screen reader as any pointer-triggered upload control.
accessibility.reducedMotion: No motion is proposed for these five copy surfaces; if entrance animation is added later it must respect prefers-reduced-motion and not gate legibility of the headline, CTA, or empty-state text.
